blockers.title: basedOn.claudeV1Reject cites a digest that no longer reproduces, and the artifact now at that path is an ACCEPT at 0/0/0 containing no finding by the id this candidate says it landed

blockers.finding: The candidate pins its predecessor verdict at 49988c67811e1b52344f7fca21abc72f450c8894434002525a76b528c4c7b874 and characterises it as 'Claude REJECT 0/1 CLAUDE-FCRO-V1-SF1', with the role field elaborating 'CLAUDE-FCRO-V1-SF1: variantsVerbatim[3] was a first-sentence truncation of v4 variants[3]. Repair: carry the whole 560-character string.' predecessorV1.role repeats 'Claude REJECT 0/1 CLAUDE-FCRO-V1-SF1', and authorityClaim and purpose both rest the whole existence of v2 on landing that finding. The dispatch pins the same digest and gives the same characterisation. Two measurements break it. First, the digest. The path measured 49988c67 on my first command of this cycle and 65fef261 on every measurement afterwards; the change happened while this review was in progress. Nine of the candidate's ten cited digests reproduce; this one does not. Second, and independent of any timing question, the content. The file now at that path carries verdict ACCEPT, blockers 0, mustFix 0, shouldFix 0, and an empty findings array, and the string CLAUDE-FCRO-V1-SF1 occurs in it zero times. So a reader who follows this candidate's own citation is told that v1 was accepted with no findings at all, while the candidate tells them v1 was rejected for a specific finding it exists to repair. I want to be exact about what I am and am not asserting, because the honest reading is narrower than it first looks. The file now at that path is a complete and coherent Claude-2-lane review of v1 that finds the SAME defect on the SAME measurements — it records variantsVerbatim item 3 as a 167-character prefix of a 560-character source, names the identical dropped sentence, and even leaves a forward note for a later revision. It classifies that defect as an observation rather than a finding and accepts at 0/0. So the two verdicts on v1 agree on every fact and differ on severity. This is a review disagreement plus an overwrite at a single-occupancy path, not a falsified measurement, and I am not alleging otherwise. What it is not is a record a later act can rely on: as things stand the corpus contains a v2 whose stated premise is a REJECT that the cited bytes do not contain.
blockers.whyItMatters: The next act is a D-000 recording. A coordinator recording v2 on the strength of basedOn.claudeV1Reject would be recording a repair against a verdict file that says the predecessor needed no repair, at a digest that does not reproduce. Every other citation in this candidate is exact, which is precisely why this one would be trusted rather than checked.
blockers.whatWouldRepairIt: This is not an authoring defect and the fix is not the author's alone. The candidate was written at 06:04 and the dispatch at 06:05, both pinning a value that was correct then; the path changed at 06:06. The coordinator has to settle which v1 verdict is the record. If the accepting verdict now on disk is the record, then v2's premise, its authorityClaim, its purpose and both provenance roles need restating — v2 becomes a voluntary improvement on an already-accepted v1, not the landing of a REJECT, and it is none the worse for that since the repair is exact. If the rejecting verdict is the record, the pinned bytes need restoring at that path. Either way v2 should be re-pinned to whichever file is the record and re-issued, and the corpus would be better served by giving the two v1 verdicts distinct paths so a single-occupancy filename stops being the thing that decides which review exists.
blockers.notAnAllegation: I make no claim about who changed the file or why, and none about bad faith. I record two measurements of one path, the content at the second measurement, and the fact that the candidate's characterisation is not satisfied by it.

For FC-RO.audit-write-fails-no-space and FC-RO.audit-write-fails-access-refused it is the same 167-character prefix of the 560-character variant that the array carried at v1, in a field whose name also says verbatim. I am deliberately not escalating this. The full text is now present in the artifact at variantsVerbatim[3], so nothing is lost; the prefix still uniquely identifies which variant the state realises, which is the field's working function; and my own v1 repair instruction expressly directed the fix to the array and blessed the per-state form, so the author executed exactly what was asked. A fresh reviewer could reasonably call it a SHOULD-FIX on the field name alone, and it closes with one edit, so it is worth closing whenever this file is next opened.

advisories.title: v2 carries no finding-disposition block, so the non-binding findings raised against v1 are neither adopted nor declined
advisories.detail: The candidate records the one SHOULD-FIX and its repair in authorityClaim, purpose and claudeV1Reject.role, and says nothing about the four advisories raised against v1 — or, if the accepting verdict is the record, about the five observations it raised. Advisories are non-binding and silence is lawful. But this corpus has the idiom: doctor-actor-leftover-join.v2 carries a findingDisposition block naming each inherited item and its disposition, which is what lets a later reviewer see at a glance what was considered and set aside rather than missed. A three-line block would remove that ambiguity permanently.

(4) FC-RO's governing pass property is carried nowhere while the variant-specific one is carried twice — defensible for an initial-state catalog, and worth noting only because that property's scope limb is what makes DEG-7 concurrent mutation scorable rather than a second grant-journal-style collision.

The subject held: 921bd720 at 0444, 13897 bytes, unmoved and unedited at both ends; HEAD never left 5d5d778; file 08 is 3a9442d1 matching the subject's own pin; required-now is 26 of 26; the frozen v1 subject is intact at 70877c0d and I did not review it. Members 0 through 2 remain exact, fcRoExactByteIntent remains exact, all seven DEG definitions remain exact, and the path diff to v1 is the smallest I have measured here: one changed value, four housekeeping fields, six added provenance paths, zero paths removed. On the repair alone this would be an ACCEPT. The blocker is custody. basedOn.claudeV1Reject pins the predecessor verdict at 49988c67 and calls it 'Claude REJECT 0/1 CLAUDE-FCRO-V1-SF1'. That path measured 49988c67 on my first command of this cycle and 65fef261 on every measurement after — it changed while this review was running. Nine of the candidate's ten cited digests reproduce; that one does not. Independently of the timing, the file now at that path carries verdict ACCEPT with blockers 0, mustFix 0, shouldFix 0 and an empty findings array, and contains the string CLAUDE-FCRO-V1-SF1 zero times. So the candidate's stated reason for existing is not supported by the bytes it cites. I want the record to be precise about what this is and is not. The file now at that path is a complete, coherent Claude-2-lane review of v1 that finds the same defect on the same measurements — it names the identical 167-of-560 prefix and the identical dropped sentence — and classifies it as an observation rather than a finding, accepting at 0/0.
